answers.answer: The document explicitly states that vCenter Server 7.0 release-note sections appear 7 times across its "Earlier Releases of vCenter Server 7.0" section list. However, across the document, 16 distinct versions of vCenter Server 7.0 are covered (vCenter Server 7.0 base, Update 1, Update 3c, Update 3d, Update 3e, Update 3m, Update 3n, Update 3o, Update 3p, Update 3q, Update 3r, Update 3s, Update 3t, Update 3u, Update 3v, and Update 3w). The discrepancy arises because the document's stated collection total of 7 refers specifically to the base "Earlier Releases" summary section, whereas individual update releases each have their own dedicated release-note sections.

page 335 / vCenter Server Update and Patch Releases

answers.answer: No, ESXi 7.0 Update 3w and vCenter Server 7.0 Update 3w do not describe the same release event. ESXi 7.0 Update 3w was released on 15 JUL 2025 with Build 24784741 (a security-only update resolving CVE-2025-2884 and CVE-2025-41226 through CVE-2025-41228), whereas vCenter Server 7.0 Update 3w was released on 29 SEP 2025 with ISO Build 24927011 (resolving CVE-2025-41250).
evidence: page 110 / VMware ESXi 7.0 Update 3w Release Notes / Introduction
page 634 / VMware vCenter Server 7.0 Update 3w Release Notes / Introduction

answers.answer: Across the ESXi 7.0 update releases, the balance shifts from mixed bug-and-security fixes toward security-only updates over time. Early in the cycle, releases such as Update 3q (May 21, 2024) include both bug and security fixes (e.g., ESXi70U3q-23794027: Security and Bugfix image), and Update 3v (May 20, 2025) bundles both security and bug fixes across multiple components. Later releases trend toward security-only: Update 3w (July 15, 2025) is explicitly designated as a "Security only image" (Build 24784741), and Update 3s (resolving CVE-2025-22224, CVE-2025-22225, and CVE-2025-22226) focuses exclusively on security vulnerability remediation.
evidence: page 111 / ESXi Image
page 114 / ESXi-7.0U3w-24784741-no-tools
page 140 / Components

answers.answer: Reading the release notes in date order, the document initially presents standard VMware product branding ("VMware vSphere 7.0", "VMware ESXi 7.0", "VMware vCenter Server 7.0"). In later 2025 release notes—specifically starting in vCenter Server 7.0 Update 3w (September 29, 2025)—the documentation references Broadcom advisories ("For more information on this vulnerability and its impact on Broadcom products..."), reflecting Broadcom's acquisition and brand management of VMware.

answers.answer: Component deprecations and removals are primarily discussed in the "Product Support Notices" section of the vSphere 7.0 Release Notes (pages 76–78), covering removals such as vCenter Server for Windows, External Platform Services Controller (PSC), built-in VNC server, and VMKLinux drivers, along with deprecations of 32-bit Userworlds, Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA), and Update Manager plugin. In later update release notes, these items are handled by enforcing native replacements (e.g., Lifecycle Manager replacing Update Manager, 64-bit userworlds, and vCenter Server Appliance with embedded PSC).
